title: Secure Medical Data Transmission Using Quantum Key Distribution and Post-Quantum Cryptography in Real-World Fiber Networks
authors: Vasile-Laurentiu Dosan, Paul Spooren, Sebastian Moeckel, Alessandro Zannotti, Alek Lagarrigue, Pablo Vazquez, Marc Bodenstein, Jonas Jelonek, Jansen Dwan, Fabian Steinlechner, Kevin Füchsel, Thomas Hühn, Oliver de Vries
abstract: The threat quantum computers pose to classical public-key cryptography motivates the deployment of quantum-safe communication for critical infrastructure such as healthcare, finance, and energy systems. Quantum key distribution (QKD) and post-quantum cryptography (PQC) offer complementary security guarantees, information-theoretic key exchange and quantum-resistant end-to-end authentication that can be combined in a layered architecture. Here, we demonstrate a field-deployed quantum-secure network integrating entanglement-based QKD with end-to-end PQC over 140 km of installed fiber in Thuringia, Germany, connecting a rural health kiosk to a university hospital via a trusted-node architecture comprising heterogeneous underground and aerial fiber links. Unlike conventional deployments that rely on a dedicated key management system to forward keys to applications, our architecture injects QKD keys directly into standard Linux-based VPN tunnels between adjacent nodes, while PQC secures the communication end-to-end, remaining fully compatible with existing infrastructure and software. Polarization-entangled photon pairs were generated at 810 nm and 1550 nm, with the telecom photon transmitted over deployed fiber. Active polarization stabilization and dispersion compensation preserve the entanglement and enable 22 days of continuous, fully autonomous operation, further underscoring the technological maturity of entanglement-based QKD approaches in a real-world fiber environment. Although the two deployed links were operated during separate rather than concurrent periods, the predominantly aerial link exhibited markedly greater instability, with QBER variations most strongly correlated with wind speed. The generated keys secured a telemedicine proof-of-concept without modifying existing medical systems, demonstrating a practical framework for quantum-safe critical infrastructures.
summary: This paper demonstrates a robust, quantum-safe communication framework by combining entanglement-based Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) with Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) over a 140 km fiber link. The system successfully secured a telemedicine proof-of-concept without modifying existing hospital infrastructure. This establishes a practical blueprint for deploying quantum-resistant security in critical real-world networks.
main_problem: The threat posed by quantum computers to classical public-key cryptography necessitates the deployment of quantum-safe communication for critical infrastructure like healthcare.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a practical, field-deployed quantum-secure telemedicine network integrating entanglement-based QKD with PQC over 140 km of real-world fiber.
method: They implemented a layered security architecture where QKD establishes link-level keys injected into VPN tunnels, while PQC secures the communication end-to-end, all without modifying existing medical systems.
model_or_system: The system uses polarization-entangled photon pairs transmitted over a heterogeneous fiber network (underground/aerial) connecting a health kiosk to a hospital. The architecture combines QKD key exchange (BBM92 protocol) with PQC key encapsulation (QuantShake1).
key_observables: Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER), coincidence rates, and the correlation between QBER fluctuations and environmental factors like wind speed.
important_parameters: 140 km fiber link length, 22 days of autonomous operation, and the use of active polarization stabilization and dispersion compensation.
main_assumptions: The layered approach assumes that QKD keys are consumed directly by the VPN layer, and PQC provides the necessary end-to-end authentication, mitigating risks associated with trusted nodes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the field-deployed network topology, the layered security architecture (QKD tunnels + PQC outer layer), and time evolution plots showing QBER and coincidence rates over the 22-day operational period.
paper_structure: The paper details the scientific motivation (quantum threat), presents the layered QKD+PQC architecture, describes the experimental setup and implementation details (photon sources, stabilization, key distillation), reports performance metrics over long-term deployment, and discusses environmental impairments.
why_interesting: While focused on networking, the work involves advanced quantum optics techniques (entangled photon sources, polarization control) and the practical application of quantum key distribution over challenging, real-world fiber links, which is highly relevant to quantum network development.
